seo.description: Pump Selection Guide Calculator — Estimate pump type selection based on flow rate, head, and fluid properties for preliminary engineering with instant results & multiple unit support.

formula.explanation: Pump selection index = Q√H. Low index (<0.1) = high head/low flow → PD or multi-stage centrifugal. High index (>0.5) = high flow/low head → single-stage centrifugal or axial.

content.introduction: Get a preliminary indication of pump type based on specific speed and viscosity. Low flow/high head favors positive displacement; high flow/medium head favors centrifugal; high viscosity favors rotary PD or gear pumps.

example.description: Pump type index based on flow/head ratio: low index (<2) suggests positive displacement, high (>20) suggests centrifugal. This is a simplified guidance only.

faq.q: When to use positive displacement pumps?
faq.a: PD pumps for: high viscosity (>500 cP), high pressure/low flow, precise metering, shear-sensitive fluids, or self-priming needs.
Specific speed Ns characterizes pump geometry: high Ns (>100) = axial/propeller; medium (30-100) = mixed flow; low (<30) = radial/centrifugal; very low = multi-stage or PD.

faq.q: How do I convert units when comparing pump curves?
faq.a: Convert head: 1 m = 3.28084 ft. Flow: 1 m³/h = 4.403 gpm. Power: 1 kW = 1.341 hp. NPSH: 1 m = 3.28084 ft. Use one consistent unit system across the entire selection to avoid curve-matching errors.

sections.heading: Unit Conversion for Pump Selection
sections.body:
**Head units**

- 1 m = 3.28084 ft
- 1 ft = 0.3048 m

**Flow units**

- 1 m³/h = 0.2778 L/s = 4.403 US gpm
- 1 US gpm = 0.2271 m³/h

**Power units**

- 1 kW = 1.341 hp
- 1 hp = 0.7457 kW

**NPSH units**

- 1 m = 3.28084 ft

Pump selection matches the duty point (flow, head) to a manufacturer curve. Convert the duty point and NPSH requirement to the same unit system as the curve before selecting.
